Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:2: "I am the Lord your God" — "blessed is the Omnipresent," etc. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: My children, I am He who set aside nine hundred and seventy-four generations before the world was created, and I came and clung to you. I am He who set aside the idol-worshiping nations of the earth and came and clung to you. I am He who set aside the whole world's idol-worshipers and chose you and called you My children and My servants. I am He of whom it is said (Isaiah 43:10), "before Me no god was formed, and after Me there shall be none," and I called you My brothers. I am He of whom it is said (ibid. 45:21), "a righteous God and a Savior, there is none besides Me," and I have made your name equal to My great Name, and My great Name equal to your name. I am He before the world was created, and I am He since the world was created; I am He in this world, and I am He in the World to Come; I put to death and I bring to life, I have wounded and I heal (Deuteronomy 32:39). — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:3: Similarly it says in the Mechilta, parashat Mishpatim (Nezikin 2), on the verse (Exodus 34:23), "Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord, the God of Israel" — our sages, of blessed memory, said: has it not already been said (Deuteronomy 16:16), "before the Lord your God"? What then does Scripture teach by "the Lord, the God of Israel"? Rather, upon Israel He unified His Name more particularly. Similarly, "Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One" (Deuteronomy 6:4) — has it not already said "the Lord our God"? What then does it teach by "the Lord is One"? Rather, upon us He unified His Name more particularly. Similarly (Jeremiah 32:36), "Therefore thus says the Lord, the God of Israel" — has it not already said "the God of all flesh"? What then does it teach by "the God of Israel"? Rather, upon Israel He unified His Name more particularly. Similarly (Psalms 50:7), "Hear, My people, and I will speak; Israel, and I will testify against you; I am God, your God" — I am God to all who come into the world, even though I have unified My Name only upon Israel. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:4: Beyond unifying His Name upon Israel to be called the God of Israel, further, out of His love for them He caused His Shechinah to dwell among them. And so Rabbi Tanchuma explained (Terumah 9) on the verse (Malachi 1:2), "I have loved you, says the Lord" — our sages expounded: it was the generation of Malachi that He spoke with, and they would answer Him. He said to them (ibid. 3:8), "Shall a man rob God?" They answered Him: how have we robbed You? Rabbi Levi said: this is Arabic idiom — when one converses with his fellow, he says to him, "you are robbing me," meaning "you are cheating me" [i.e., "kove'a" also connotes cheating]. And you said, how have we robbed You? — in the tithes and the terumah that are not given out properly. He returned and said to them: was not Esau a brother to Jacob? And you said, how have You loved us? It is the way of the world that whoever has two sons, one the firstborn and one the younger, who receives more? The firstborn. Esau emerged first, as it is said (Genesis 25:25), "and the first one emerged red," and he ought to have received two portions, yet I did not do so — rather, Jacob received two portions, this world and the World to Come, while Esau received only this world. See how I have loved you: from earth to the firmament is a five-hundred-year journey, and likewise from the first firmament to the second, from the second to the third, from the third to the fourth, from the fourth to the fifth, from the fifth to the sixth, from the sixth to the seventh — and there is no need to estimate from the hooves of the Chayot [creatures], with the Throne above all of them — and see how I have cherished you, that I set aside all of these and said to you, make for Me curtains of goats' hair, as it is said (Exodus 25:8), "and let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:5: Further, in Midrash Tanchuma (Kedoshim 5), that out of the Holy One, blessed be He's, love for Israel He called them by His own name, in these words: "For as a girdle clings to the loins of a man, so have I caused the whole house of Israel to cling to Me" (Jeremiah 13:11). The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I am not like flesh and blood — flesh and blood does not permit a commoner to be called by the king's own name, but Israel is called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Every beloved name by which the Holy One, blessed be He, is called, He called Israel by it: He is called "Elohim," and He called Israel "Elohim," as it is said (Psalms 82:6), "I said, you are gods." He is called "wise," as it is said (Job 9:4), "wise of heart and mighty in strength," and He called Israel "wise," as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:6), "surely this is a wise and understanding people." He is called "Beloved [Dod]," as it is said (Song of Songs 5:10), "my Beloved is radiant and ruddy," and He called Israel "beloved ones [dodim]," as it is said (Song of Songs 5:1), "eat, friends, drink and be drunk with love [dodim]." He is called "chosen one [bachur]," as it is said (Song of Songs 5:15), "his appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars," and He called Israel "chosen ones," as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:2), "and the Lord your God has chosen you [bacharu]." He is called "pious [chasid]," as it is said (Jeremiah 3:12), "for I am pious [chasid], says the Lord," and He called Israel "pious," as it is said (Psalms 50:5), "gather to Me My pious ones [chasidai]." He is called "holy," and Israel are called "holy," as it is said (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I am holy." And even in the future to come, each and every one will be called "holy," as it is said (Isaiah 4:3), "and it shall come to pass, whoever remains in Zion and is left in Jerusalem shall be called holy." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:6: Similarly, they said in the Zohar (parashat Mishpatim 121a): happy are Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to honor them above all other peoples of the world. First He said to them (Exodus 19:6), "and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests" — and He did not withhold His abundant love from them until He called them also "a holy nation," which is greater; He did not withhold His love from them until He called them (Deuteronomy 7:6), "for you are a holy people"; He did not withhold His love from them until He called them (Exodus 22:30), "and you shall be holy men to Me," which is greater than all. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:7: Further the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (parashat Shemot 20a) — he said there — that everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created above among the supernal beings, He created below, so that the worlds would be one unity. And he said afterward: He created the angels above; He created human beings in this world; He created the Leviathan in the sea, corresponding to (Exodus 36:18), "to join the tent together, to be one." It is written of man (Genesis 9:6), "for in the image of God He made man," and it is written (Psalms 8:6), "and You have made him a little less than God" — if human beings are so precious in their deeds, all this, and they are formed from a mere drop from a cistern, from which many come to draw. And He chose the supernal beings, and He chose Israel; the supernal beings He did not call "children," but the ones below He called "children" — this is what is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the Lord your God." He called them children, and they called Him Father, as it is written (Isaiah 63:16), "for You are our Father"; and it is written (Song of Songs 2:16), "my Beloved is mine and I am His" — He chose me and I chose Him. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:8: On this aspect it says in the Mishnah (Avot 2): beloved are Israel, for they are called children to the Omnipresent, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the Lord your God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:9: Further, in the Midrash Yelamdenu, on the verse "you are children to the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 14:1) — that the angels are called by five names of affection, and by all of them the Holy One, blessed be He, called Israel, cherishing them even more than the ministering angels; quoted in the Yalkut (parashat Re'eh, siman 891, p. 278) on the verse "you are children," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:10: And further there, subsequently: the Rashbi said, see with how many terms the Holy One, blessed be He, cherished Israel — He called them children, and He returned and called them a holy nation in this very passage, and three times in this passage He unified His Name upon them: "you are children to the Lord your God"; "for you are a holy people to the Lord your God"; "and the Lord your God has chosen you" (14:1-2). The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: in this world I have chosen you and unified My Name upon you; in the future to come I shall walk among you in My glory, "and I will walk among you." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:11: Further, on the matter of the Holy One, blessed be He's, love, it says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Rabbah, ch. 28) — and this is the end of the passage we quoted in chapter 1 of this Gate — in these words: this is what Scripture says (Song of Songs 8:7), "many waters cannot extinguish the love" — the house of Israel, I atone for them in all the places of their dwellings, for they neither circumcise nor read nor study except out of love for their Father in Heaven — for the Holy One, blessed be He, says to Israel: My children, I swear by My Throne of Glory that even if the idol-worshiping nations of the world should arise and offer money, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:12: Further, on the matter of the Holy One, blessed be He's, love for Israel, our sages, of blessed memory, said in Pesikta Rabbati (siman 40), in these words: "remind Me, let us go to judgment together" (Isaiah 43:26) — this is what Scripture says (ibid. 42:21), "the Lord desires, for the sake of His righteousness," and so it says (ibid. 63:1), "I speak in righteousness." The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I desire that you be vindicated in judgment. Come and see: two enter into judgment — this one silences his opponent, saying, I am first, and his fellow does not let him, saying, I am first. But the Holy One, blessed be He, when He said to Israel, come let us go to judgment together, as it is written, "remind Me, let us go to judgment together," said: who shall speak first? The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: you speak first — "recount, that you may be vindicated" (ibid. 43:26). Why? If I defeat you in judgment, it is I who lose out; but if you defeat Me, I gain. I defeated the generation of the Flood — I lost all that population, "and He blotted out all existence" (Genesis 7:23). Moses defeated Me — "and He said He would destroy them, had not Moses His chosen one" (Psalms 106:23) — I gained. This is what is written (Psalms 4:1), "for the conductor [la-menatze'ach], a psalm" — sing to the One who is defeated [menutzach], and He rejoices. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:13: And in the Zohar (parashat Balak 203b) they spoke of the matter of the Holy One, blessed be He's, love, a subject related to the previous passage, in these words: he opened and said (Micah 6:5), "My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised" — "My people": how merciful is the Holy One, blessed be He, toward His children — for although they sinned against Him in all their ways, He is like a father toward his son: if the son sins against his father, he strikes him — so much so that he strikes him and he does not turn from his way, he rebukes him with words and he does not accept it — the father says, I do not wish to do to my son what I have done until today; if I strike him, he will ache in his head, and behold, that pain of his is with me; if I rebuke him harshly, behold his appearance changes — what shall I do? Rather, let me go and beg him and speak soft words to him, so that he not become sad. So in every manner the Holy One, blessed be He, deals with Israel — He began to strike them and they did not accept it. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I see in My son that because of the striking with which I struck them, they ache in their heads — woe, for through their pain I too ache, as it is written (Isaiah 63:9), "in all their distress He was distressed"; I rebuked them and their appearance changed, as it is written (Lamentations 4:8), "their appearance is blacker than soot, they are not recognized in the streets" — woe, when I look at them and they are not recognizable! Now I will beg them with supplications: My people, what have I done to you, and how have I wearied you? My only son, beloved of My soul, what have I done to you? I gave you dominion over all the members of My palace, I gave you dominion over all the kings of the worlds; and if I have done other things to you, let it answer for Me — you be witness for Me. "My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and how Balaam son of Beor answered him" — "remember now": be mindful, I beg of you, of what he devised. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:14: Similarly, it says in Midrash Tanchuma on the verse (Numbers 23:8), "How shall I curse whom God has not cursed?" — in these words: at the time they [Israel] deserved to be cursed, they were not cursed; but when Jacob came in to receive the blessings, as it is written (Genesis 27:16), "and the skins of the kids of the goats," etc., his father said to him, who are you? He said to him, I am Esau your firstborn. One who utters a falsehood from his mouth ought to be cursed — yet not only was he not cursed, but he was blessed, for it is said, "indeed he shall be blessed" — how then could I curse him? This is "God has not cursed."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:15: Another interpretation: it is the way of the world that a legion that rebels against the king forfeits its life; yet these denied and rebelled against Him, saying, "these are your gods, O Israel," and were not fit for annihilation — even at that hour His affection for them did not depart, but He accompanied them with the clouds of glory, the manna, and the well. So it says (Nehemiah 9:18), "even when they made themselves a molten calf," etc., "yet You, in Your great mercies, did not forsake them," etc., "and the manna You did not withhold from their mouths" — how then could I curse them?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:16: When He commands them concerning the blessings and the curses — regarding the blessings He mentions them by name, as it is said (Deuteronomy 27:12), "these shall stand to bless the people"; but regarding the curses, He did not personally demand them, as it is said (ibid. 27:13), "and these shall stand for the curse." Moreover, when they sin and He says to bring a curse upon them, it is not written that He Himself brings it; but with the blessings, He Himself blesses them, as it says (ibid. 28:1-2), "and it shall come to pass, if you diligently listen... the Lord your God will set you on high... the Lord will command upon you the blessing"; whereas with the curses it is written (ibid. 28:15), "and it shall come to pass, if you do not listen... they will come upon you" — of themselves. Hence, "How shall I curse whom God has not cursed?" — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:17: Since we see that the Holy One, blessed be He, desires the blessing and praise of Israel, a person must always plead their defense and never their prosecution. So it is said in Yelamdenu regarding Gideon: when it was said to him (Judges 6:14), "go in this strength of yours" — Rabbi Yehudah bar Shalom said, that night was the night of Passover, the very night he was told (ibid. 6:13), "and where are all His wonders?" — where are the wonders that God performed for our forefathers on this very night, when He smote the firstborn of Egypt and brought Israel out from there rejoicing? And since he pleaded Israel's defense, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: it is right that I reveal Myself to him in My glory upon him, as it is said, "and the Lord turned to him and said, go in this strength of yours" — the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: you have the strength to plead Israel's defense; by your merit they are redeemed, as it is said, "and you shall save Israel." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:18: Further, in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Zuta, ch. 8), on the verse (I Kings 19:9), "What are you doing here, Elijah?" — in these words: "what are you doing here, Elijah?" He should have said before Him: Master of the universe, Your children are the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who did Your will in Your world. He did not do so, but said, "I have been very jealous," etc. The Holy One, blessed be He, began to speak words of comfort with him. He said: when I descended to give the Torah to Israel, none descended with Me but the ministering angels who wished them well, as it is said (ibid. 19:11), "go and stand upon the mountain," etc., "and after the earthquake, a fire." He waited for him three hours, and he still remained in his original words, saying, "I have been very jealous." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him (ibid. 19:16), "and Elisha son of Shaphat you shall anoint as prophet in your place" — what you have in mind, you cannot accomplish. He said to him, You are always jealous. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:19: Further, out of the Holy One, blessed be He's, love, He causes His Shechinah to dwell with them even in exile, as they elaborated in the Zohar, parashat Bechukotai (115b), on the verse (Leviticus 26:44), "and yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not despise them nor abhor them" — and He is called "saved" through their redemption, as it is said (Zechariah 9:9), "righteous and saved," etc., as elaborated in Midrash Tanchuma at the end of parashat Acharei Mot (siman 12).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:20: Further they said in the Midrash (Mishlei) on "in the multitude of people is the King's glory" (Proverbs 14:28): Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said, to tell the praise and greatness of the Holy One, blessed be He — although He has a thousand thousands and countless myriads upon myriads of companies of ministering angels to serve Him and praise Him, He desires only the praise of Israel, as it is said, "in the multitude of people is the King's glory," and "people" [am] refers only to Israel, as it is said (Isaiah 43:21), "this people [am] I have formed for Myself" — why? "That they might declare My praise." So too it says (Psalms 47:10), "the willing ones of the peoples are gathered, the people of the God of Abraham." Rabbi Simon said: the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted in His world when Israel gather in synagogues and study halls and give praise, thanksgiving, and greatness to the Holy One, blessed be He. And Rabbi Yishmael said: at that moment, when they hear the Aggadah from the mouth of a sage and afterward answer, "Amen, may His great Name be blessed," at that moment the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices and says to the ministering angels: come and see the people I formed for Myself, how they praise Me! At that moment He is clothed in splendor and majesty; therefore it says, "in the multitude of people is the King's glory," "but in the lack of a nation is the ruin of a prince" — if they cease from words of Torah, I too will withhold from them the proofs of Torah. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:21: Of the things that arouse [love], a person should remember how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for us and showed us His love — first at the Exodus from Egypt, regarding the plagues that afflicted Egypt specifically. The plague of blood was blood for the Egyptians and water for Israel; likewise, in the plague of pestilence (Exodus 9:4), "and the Lord shall distinguish between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, and nothing of all that belongs to the children of Israel shall die." Third, in the plague of darkness (ibid. 10:23), "but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings" — wherever an Israelite went, the light went with him, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Shemot Rabbah 14:3). Further, in the plague of the firstborn (ibid. 11:7), "but against any of the children of Israel not a dog shall sharpen its tongue." And the command regarding the placing of the blood was a kind of protective sign, alluding to the three yods, which is mercy, and it says (Exodus 12:23), "and he will not permit the destroyer to come [into your houses to smite you]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:22: Likewise Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, admonished Israel in Mishneh Torah (Deuteronomy 4:34), "Or has any god ventured to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of a nation, by trials, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that the Lord your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes." And our sages, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash on the passage of the manna (Yalkut, siman 258), on what is written (Exodus 16:6), "and you shall know that the Lord brought you out of the land of Egypt": from here you learn that the Exodus from Egypt is equal in weight to all the miracles and mighty deeds the Omnipresent performed for Israel. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:23: Further they said in Bamidbar Rabbah, on the verse (Numbers 14:27), "how long shall I bear with this evil congregation" — the Holy One, blessed be He, said, as it were: a person acquires a servant so that the servant may carry the lantern and light the way for his master; but I did not do so — rather, you are My servants (Leviticus 25:55), "for the children of Israel are servants to Me," and I carry the lantern and light the way for you. — end of quotation. The interpretation of "lantern" is a metaphor for the pillar of fire that lit for them at night. In truth, the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night correspond to the attribute of day and the attribute of night, whose respective partners are Chesed and Din, and both together are YHVH-Elohim; and this shows the strength of His love, blessed be He, for us — though those who hold only to the plain meaning, lacking knowledge of the inner secret of the Torah, do not sense this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:24: And it further says there: another interpretation — it is the way of the world that when a person acquires a servant, if he goes on a journey, his servant goes ahead of him and prepares lodging for him; but I did not do so — rather, you are My servants, and I prepared the lodging for you, as it is said (Numbers 10:33), "and the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord," etc., "to seek out a resting place for them."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:25: Another interpretation: it is the way of the world that when a person acquires a servant, his servant bakes bread for him; but I did not do so — you are My servants, and I baked bread for you from heaven, as it says (Psalms 78:25), "man ate the bread of the mighty."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:26: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: let Me destroy them from before Me. Moses said before Him: Master of the universe, You are slow to anger — and if a servant's deeds are good and he listens to his master, and his master looks upon him with a favorable countenance, one does not credit the master with kindness; but when is credit given? When the servant is of evil upbringing and his master still looks upon him with a favorable countenance. So too, You — do not look upon the stiffness of their neck, as it is said (Deuteronomy 9:27), "do not turn to the stubbornness of this people." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: for your sake I will forgive them, as it is said (Numbers 14:20), "and the Lord said, I have forgiven, according to your word." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:27: Immediately following this, it explains there that all the things a father is obligated to do for his son, the Holy One, blessed be He, did for Israel — a father is obligated to redeem him, to teach him Torah, to anoint him and clothe him — all these He did for Israel; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:28: They said in the Midrash (Midrash of Three and Four, siman 58; Tanchuma, Beshalach 10), on the verse (Exodus 14:16), "and you, lift up your staff," regarding the splitting of the Sea of Reeds — that our sages, of blessed memory, said ten miracles were performed at it, in these words: ten miracles were performed for Israel at the Sea. The waters split and formed a kind of dome, as it is said (Habakkuk 3:14), "You pierced with his own rods." It was divided into two, as it is said (Exodus 14:26), "stretch out your hand over the sea and split it." It became dry land, as it is said (ibid. 14:29), "and the children of Israel walked on dry land." It became like clay, as it is said (Habakkuk 3:15), "You trod through the sea with Your horses, through the heap of great waters." It broke into crumbs, as it is said (Psalms 74:13), "You broke the sea by Your strength." It became rocks, as it is said (ibid.), "You broke the heads of the sea-monsters upon the waters." It became cut sections, as it is said (ibid. 136:13), "to Him who divided the Sea of Reeds into sections." It formed heaps, as it is said (Exodus 15:8), "and with the breath of Your nostrils the waters were piled up." It became like a wall, as it is said (ibid.), "the flowing waters stood upright like a wall." Sweet waters came forth for them out of the salty, as it is said (Psalms 78:16), "and He brought forth flowing waters from the rock." The sea congealed into two parts and became like a kind of glass mirror, as it is said (Exodus 15:8), "the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:29: Further, one should contemplate and examine the miracle performed for them at the Jordan when they entered the Land. Our sages, of blessed memory, said there (Sotah 34a; Yalkut, Yehoshua, siman 14): how wide was the water — twelve miles by twelve miles, corresponding to the camp of Israel. Rabbi Elazar said to Rabbi Shimon: according to your words, is a man swift or is water swift? Surely water is swift — if so, the waters would come and sweep them away! Rather, this teaches that the waters were piled up, wave upon wave, for more than three hundred miles, until all the kings of east and west saw them, as it is said (Joshua 5:1), "and it came to pass, when [all the kings of the Amorites... and all the kings of the Canaanites] heard," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:30: Further, in recounting the miracle, it says further (Yalkut): our rabbis taught: when the last of Israel came up out of the Jordan, the waters returned to their place, as it is said (Joshua 4:18), "and it came to pass, when the priests bearing the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord came up out of the midst of the Jordan," etc. — it turns out that the Ark and its bearers were on one side and Israel on the other side; the Ark carried its bearers and crossed over, as it is said (ibid. 4:11), "and it came to pass, when all the people had finished crossing over, that the Ark of the Lord crossed over, and the priests, before the people." For this matter Uzzah was punished, as it is said (II Samuel 6:6-7), "and Uzzah put out his hand to the Ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled, and the anger of the Lord burned against Uzzah" — the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Uzzah, it carries its own bearers — how much more so itself! — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:31: Our sages, peace be upon them, instituted for us the blessing "by whose word all things came to be" and "Creator of many souls" over the drinking of water, so that we would remember the miracles performed for us regarding water — and this is proven in Devarim Rabbah, parashat Ekev, in these words: (Deuteronomy 9:1), "Hear, O Israel, you are crossing the Jordan today" — the halachah is: a person from Israel who drinks water for his thirst says, "Blessed is He by whose word all things came to be." Rabbi Tarfon says: "Creator of many souls and their deficiencies." Our rabbis say: come and see — all the miracles that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel, He performed them only through water. How so? While they were still in Egypt He performed miracles for them at the river — Rabbi Yitzchak said, the Egyptians and Israel would go to drink water from the river; the Egyptian drank blood and the Israelite drank water. And when they went out of Egypt, the Holy One, blessed be He, performed miracles only through water — from where do we know this? As it is said (Psalms 114:3), "the sea saw and fled." What did it see? Rabbi Nehorai said, the Explicit Name was engraved upon the staff, and it split, as it is said (Psalms 77:17), "the waters saw You and were in anguish." They came to Marah when they came up from the sea and the waters were bitter; there He performed miracles for them — from where do we know this? As it is said (Exodus 15:25), "and the Lord showed him a tree," etc. At the rock He performed miracles for them with water, as it is said (Numbers 20:8), "and speak to the rock," etc. At the well He performed miracles for them and they sang a song, as it is said (ibid. 21:17), "then Israel sang." Moses said to them: know that all the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for you, He performed only through water; even when you cross the Jordan to inherit the Land, He is destined to perform miracles for you through the waters of the Jordan. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:32: Now what needs examination in this passage is obvious: what connection is there between beginning with "the halachah is: a person from Israel who drinks water for his thirst," and the verse "Hear, O Israel"? And the rabbis' saying, "come and see all the miracles He performed," is connected with the preceding blessings, in particular "Creator of many souls."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:33: Rather, the matter is that the author of this passage sensed a difficulty in the verse — what does Moses come to teach us by saying "you are crossing the Jordan today"? And the intent of the resolution of this difficulty is what is stated at the end of the passage, that the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to perform miracles for them through the waters of the Jordan; and in order to explain this matter, he was compelled to introduce this entire preamble.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:34: And he said: the halachah is, a person from Israel who drinks water for his thirst blesses "shehakol" — and this is as if to inform us and hint to us the reason why they instituted this blessing over water in this wording, "by whose word all things came to be," without specifying "water" in it as in the wording of the other blessings, such as "Who creates the fruit of the tree" — and one would have expected it to say that He created the water. Further, Rabbi Tarfon says "Creator of many souls and their deficiencies" — why did Rabbi Tarfon inform us of this matter regarding water more than other things? And by strict law, anything whose opening blessing is "shehakol," such as things that do not grow from the ground, has as its closing blessing "many souls"; moreover, the wording of the blessing "Creator of many souls and their deficiencies" is an all-encompassing blessing, and so the Tur wrote, Orach Chaim, siman 207, that the meaning of "Creator of many souls and their deficiencies" is all that they lack, and Rabbeinu Yonah wrote that it is in the language of "all your want is upon Me" — meaning the need — and regarding all the other things He created in the world, which serve only for pleasure, "to give life to the soul of every living thing, blessed be the Life of the worlds" is attached to the end of the blessing, for all that He created. If so, let us return to our question: since this blessing is an all-encompassing one, why is its particular case regarding water mentioned?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:35: These two difficulties our sages, of blessed memory, intended to resolve, and they said: come and see, all the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel, He performed them only through water — and one must examine these words carefully, for it is impossible in any way to understand them literally, since several miracles were performed for Israel that had nothing to do with water. In Egypt, of the eight plagues [not counting blood and hail], water had no part except in the plague of blood and the plague of hail; and afterward, the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night, the giving of manna and quail, the giving of the Torah in fire, the war against Amalek, the wars against Sichon and Og, and the many miracles Elijah and Elisha performed that had nothing to do with water — how so?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:36: Rather, without doubt the intent is that all the miracles performed were performed only from the side of simple Chesed, and they were likened to water — for water is the sustenance of the world, this being what is written (Psalms 104:3), "who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters," and it is written (ibid. 89:3), "I said, the world shall be built with kindness" — and therefore the world cannot exist without water.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:37: Therefore he brought all these miracles that were performed through water, for all the miracles themselves indicate the aspect of Chesed. How so? At the river, Israel drank water and the Egyptian drank blood — this is the aspect of Chesed; and because of its connection with Gevurah, it was blood for the Egyptian; and the rest of the distinctions are self-explanatory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:38: He said at the end of the passage, "even when you cross the Jordan" — so that you should not say that the attribute of Chesed was employed only until their arrival in the Land. There is also proof of this in Vayikra Rabbah, parashat "And when you shall plant every food-tree" (Leviticus 19:23); see there. This informs us that even as they crossed the Jordan to inherit the Land, the aspect of Chesed went there with them. This is what the verse means (Deuteronomy 9:1), "you [atah] are crossing the Jordan today" — for the word "atah" is superfluous, since it already said "Hear, O Israel," and moreover it should have said "you [plural] are crossing." Rather, the intent is regarding the attribute of Chesed, called "Atah" (Psalms 110:4), "You [Atah] are a priest forever" — it is He who crosses the Jordan with you, to perform for you a miracle through the waters of the Jordan.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:39: The reason that the miracles are attributed to Chesed is that a miracle is a change in nature, and "teva" [nature] has the same numerical value as "Elohim." Now, the attribute of Gevurah, which is [called] Elohim, employs the lower attribute of Elohim [Malchut], and the creation of the world was through judgment, "In the beginning God [Elohim] created" (Genesis 1:1); "even My hand has founded the earth, and My right hand has spread out the heavens" (Isaiah 48:13). It follows that the change of nature comes from the side of Chesed and mercy, and the attribute of Righteousness [Tzaddik] is called "nes" [miracle], as explained in the Tikkunim. It occurs to me that the reason is that its secret is that "kol" ["all"] in heaven and earth has the numerical value of 110, which is the same as the value of MaH and Adonai — and this unification is from the side of Chesed, namely Eloha, spelled Aleph-Lamed-Vav-Heh, as explained in parashat Vayikra (23b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:40: With this introduction we may understand these blessings that our sages, of blessed memory, instituted over water. The reason it says "shehakol nihyah bidvaro" ["by whose word all things came to be"] is that the intent of "hakol" [all/everything] means all the miracles performed for us all "came to be by His word" — namely, through Chesed. And he said "shehakol" [that all] because the miracles come from the attribute of "KoL" — [an allusion to] "KoL" that passes among those counted [Yesod/Kol as the covenant]. And they said "shehakol" contains the letters of "heh" [alluding] "all is Heh," as explained there in the Tikkunim. And all the miracles are performed through the bond of the miracle with Chesed, and this is "nihyah bidvaro" ["came to be by His word"].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:41: There is no difficulty in the word "bidvaro" ["by His word"] being associated with Chesed, for we already find the words "davar" and "dvaro" associated with Chesed, as it says (Psalms 107:20), "He sent forth His word and healed them," and likewise (Psalms 130:5), "I have hoped for the Lord, my soul has hoped, and for His word I have waited"; "He sends forth His word and melts them" (ibid. 147:18) — the melting of the snows is from the side of Chesed, as explained in parashat Bereishit (29b). And likewise, "who can utter [yidaber] a word before Him" (Job 11:5); "for He speaks [yedaber] to one" (ibid. 33:14); (Psalms 85:9) "let me hear what God the Lord will speak [yedaber], for He will speak [yedaber] peace." And likewise speech is compared to water, as it is said (Proverbs 18:4), "deep waters are the words of a man's mouth"; "the opening of Your words gives light" (Psalms 119:130) — and "gives light" is Chesed, surely light.
